entries.title: 10-Yard Fight
entries.summary: Top-down, vertically scrolling American football game ported from Irem's 1983 arcade original. Unlike the arcade game, which only simulates offense, the NES version lets you play both offense and defense and adds simultaneous two-player games.
entries.why_it_matters: One of only two NES launch titles not originally developed by Nintendo (the other is Kung Fu); Nintendo published it in North America in 1985.
entries.gameplay_notes: No play-calling: on offense you take the snap and run with the quarterback, pitch to a running back or throw long. On defense you control one of two players while the CPU handles the rest. Punts and field goals are available. Five difficulty tiers run from high school to Super Bowl.

difficulty.reason: Winning at one tier advances you to a harder one, up to the Super Bowl level.

entries.summary: Vertically scrolling World War II shooter, ported to the NES by Micronics from Capcom's 1984 arcade hit. You fly a P-38 Lightning across the Pacific, shooting down waves of Japanese aircraft on the way to Tokyo.
entries.why_it_matters: First game in Capcom's 194X series. The NES version sold over one million copies worldwide and also ran in arcades on Nintendo's PlayChoice-10.
entries.gameplay_notes: Shoot down enemy planes and dodge fire; one hit costs a life. Power-ups include two escort fighters. A roll button loops your plane briefly out of danger. Tracks both a high score and a shoot-down percentage.

difficulty.reason: One hit loses a life, and the loop roll is the main defensive tool.

entries.title: 1943: The Battle of Midway
entries.summary: Capcom's NES version of its 1987 arcade sequel to 1942. You pilot a P-38 against Japanese air and naval forces at Midway, ending with a fight against the battleship Yamato.
entries.why_it_matters: The NES version adds its own twist: permanent stat upgrades for firepower, defense, fuel and special weapons, which changes how the game balances compared with the arcade original.
entries.gameplay_notes: Vertical shooter where fuel doubles as health. Special attacks cost fuel; pressing both buttons performs a loop. Stages alternate between carrier/battleship bosses and bomber squadrons. NES-exclusive upgrade points unlock weapons and extend special-weapon duration.

difficulty.reason: Long stages with fuel-as-health and demanding bosses.

entries.title: The 3-D Battles of WorldRunner
entries.summary: Forward-scrolling pseudo-3D action game from Square, originally a Famicom Disk System title ported to cartridge for Acclaim's NES release. As Jack the WorldRunner you run into the screen across eight worlds, jumping chasms and blasting alien Serpentbeasts.
entries.why_it_matters: Designed by Hironobu Sakaguchi and Nasir Gebelli with music by Nobuo Uematsu (later core Final Fantasy staff); one of the earliest stereoscopic 3-D games.
entries.gameplay_notes: Third-person view behind the character. Clear each world's quadrants before the timer runs out, collect power-ups from columns (such as invincibility or laser missiles), and defeat a serpent boss at the end of each world.

difficulty.reason: Timed quadrants and bottomless canyons demand precise jumping.

entries.hltb_note: No NES HLTB entry could be matched (HLTB search is not accessible to automated tools; only Wikidata-linked or title-matched ids were used).
entries.collecting_notes: North American copies included a pair of anaglyph 3D glasses for the optional 3D mode (Japanese copies sold them separately).
entries.content_notes: Optional anaglyph 3D mode uses the included red/cyan glasses; fully playable without them. Box art shortens the title to "3-D WorldRunner".

entries.summary: NES port of Atari Games' 1986 arcade skateboarding game, released by Mindscape in 1989. You skate around Skate City and enter four skate parks to earn points, medals and cash.
entries.why_it_matters: Adapts one of the first skateboarding arcade games; its "SKATE OR DIE!" killer-bee timer is its best-known feature.
entries.gameplay_notes: Skate between events in Skate City; tickets grant entry to the parks. Four classes of four events each: Ramp, Downhill, Slalom and Jump, sixteen in all. A timer runs between events; when it expires, killer bees chase you until you reach a park. Winnings buy equipment upgrades and medals are awarded.

difficulty.reason: The bee timer keeps constant pressure on you.

entries.title: 8 Eyes
entries.summary: Castlevania-style action platformer by Thinking Rabbit, published in North America by Taxan. Orin the Falconer and his fighting falcon Cutrus storm the castles of eight dukes to recover the eight jewels known as the 8 Eyes.
entries.why_it_matters: Unusual for its co-op design: a second player controls Orin's falcon, Cutrus. Its large soundtrack by Kenzou Kumei has three pieces per level.
entries.gameplay_notes: Pick the first seven castles in any order; each boss is weak to only one sword, so order matters, and hints are hidden throughout. The final stage opens after the rest, and the jewels must then be placed in the correct order or the game is lost.

difficulty.reason: In single-player you control Orin and the falcon at once, which the source says significantly increases difficulty.

entries.title: Abadox: The Deadly Inner War
entries.summary: Horizontally scrolling shooter in the vein of Gradius and R-Type, released in North America by Milton Bradley. You fly into the body of the planet-eating organism Parasitis to rescue Princess Maria, fighting through organ-themed stages.
entries.why_it_matters: Frequently noted by critics for its difficulty. Some stages break convention by scrolling downward rather than sideways.
entries.gameplay_notes: Collect speed, weapon (3-way, spread, laser, ring) and shield/option power-ups. Dying strips all upgrades and returns you to a checkpoint at base speed. Stages 2, 4 and 6 switch to downward vertical scrolling.

difficulty.reason: Single-hit deaths and loss of all power-ups on death.

entries.title: The Adventures of Bayou Billy
entries.summary: Konami beat 'em up in which Louisiana vigilante Bayou Billy fights through nine stages, from the swamps to Bourbon Street, to rescue Annabelle from crime boss Godfather Gordon.
entries.why_it_matters: Mixes three styles in one cartridge: side-scrolling brawling, light-gun shooting and driving stages.

entries.summary: Wisdom Tree's unlicensed Christian game with three Old Testament stories: Noah's Ark, Baby Moses and David and Goliath, played as Super Mario Bros. 2-style side-scrollers.
entries.why_it_matters: Sold only through Christian bookstores rather than video game outlets. It bypassed the NES lockout chip with a voltage spike at power-on.
entries.gameplay_notes: Noah's Ark: carry animals and food to the ark, reading Bible verses to heal. Baby Moses: carry the infant Moses past enemies trying to throw him in the Nile. David and Goliath: herd sheep, stun predators with acorns, then face Goliath with a sling.

entries.title: Big Nose the Caveman
entries.summary: Side-scrolling platformer by Optimus Software, released on NES by Camerica. The hungry caveman Big Nose crosses four islands (Paradise, Monster, Terror and Chaos) in search of dinner.
entries.gameplay_notes: Collect bones to buy spells, upgrades and items in shops. Stones fired from Big Nose's club protect him; without them he dies in one hit. He can't swim, and there are many pits, traps and lava.

difficulty.reason: The source notes it is long, with one-hit deaths and no restarting from checkpoints once all lives are lost.

entries.title: Bigfoot
entries.summary: Acclaim monster-truck racing game developed by Beam Software. You drive the famous truck Bigfoot through car crushing, mud bogs, tractor pulls, hill climbs and drag races.
entries.gameplay_notes: Head-to-head events against CPU trucks (The Growler, The Charger and others, which drop out when they run out of money), linked by cross-country races where you collect money and avoid damage. In two-player mode the second player drives a red truck.

entries.title: Bionic Commando
entries.summary: Capcom's NES platformer based on its 1987 arcade game. Commando Ladd uses a grappling bionic arm, rather than jumping, to rescue Super Joe and stop the Empire's Albatros project.
entries.why_it_matters: One of the few platformers where you cannot jump: every gap and ledge is crossed with the bionic arm.
entries.gameplay_notes: Move a helicopter around an overworld map. Intercepts trigger overhead Commando-style shooting stages, the only place to earn continues. In side-scrolling areas, find communication rooms, then destroy the boss-guarded computer core. Neutral zones hold information; firing there sets off an alarm. Gear found in areas unlocks progress.

difficulty.reason: Grapple-only movement takes practice, and continues are scarce.

entries.title: The Black Bass
entries.summary: HOT-B bass fishing game: advance through tournaments at four lakes by catching many heavy bass between sunrise and sunset.
entries.why_it_matters: The first Black Bass game released outside Japan (sequel to a Japan-only MSX/Famicom game). The North American title screen reads 'The Black Bass USA'.
entries.gameplay_notes: Overhead fishing: cast using a power meter, work the lure to entice bites, then reel carefully so the line doesn't snap. Lure choice depends on weather and time of day. Passwords after each tournament.

entries.title: Blades of Steel
entries.summary: Konami's arcade-style ice hockey game with fictional teams from real North American cities, famous for its on-ice fights.
entries.why_it_matters: A well-remembered NES sports game; re-released on the Wii Virtual Console in 2007.
entries.gameplay_notes: Exhibition or a playoff-style tournament for the Cup, with three CPU difficulty levels. Bump the same opponent three times to start a fight; the loser goes to the penalty box, creating a power play. Tied games go to a shootout. An intermission mini-game advertises other Konami games.

entries.title: Blaster Master
entries.summary: Sunsoft's platformer and run-and-gun. Jason follows his mutated pet frog underground and pilots the tank SOPHIA THE 3RD against radioactive mutants across eight levels.
entries.why_it_matters: Frequently ranked among the best NES games (Nintendo Power's top 100, IGN's top NES list, and second on Paste's list). Its Western story was a localisation of the Japanese game Metafight.
entries.gameplay_notes: Two modes: side-scrolling tank sections (cannon plus limited homing missiles, Thunder Break and Multi Warhead) and top-down on-foot dungeons, where your gun weakens when you take damage. Beating bosses gives the tank new abilities (hover, underwater, wall climbing). Backtracking is non-linear.

difficulty.reason: Criticised for high difficulty and no passwords or saves.
